test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-II Official Paper-I (Held On: 20 Jan, 2025)
subject: general
question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below. While the first and the last sentences (1 and 6) are in the correct order, the sentences in between are jumbled up. Arrange the sentences in the
 correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

1. There are some backward areas in Andhra Pradesh.

A. Rayalaseema is one of them.

B. Ma
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph starts by mentioning backward areas in Andhra Pradesh.
 
• **Sentence A follows** since it identifies one of such backward areas: 
 
 
• "Rayalaseema is one of them."
 
 
 
• **Sentence B is next** because it explains the result of degradation in Rayalaseema: 
 
 
• "Massive degradation of natural resources and extensive changes in land use have resulted in poor crop productivity in Rayalaseema."
 
 
 
• **Sentence D follows** as it elaborates on the technical details of soil degradation: 
 
 
• "Soil Organic Carbon (SOC), which is crucial for maintaining soil quality, has decreased by 84% in the region. Poor soil fertility and soil degradation, like in Rayalaseema region, are the major causes of food shortage."
 
 
 
• **Sentence C is the last** before the concluding sentence as it introduces the efforts of the National Soil Survey and Land use planning organisation: 
 
 
• "The National Soil Survey and Land use planning organisation is doing its job by giving suggestions to the farmers of Rayalaseema."
 
 
 
• The concluding sentence (6) ties back to the suggestions provided.
 
• The correct sequence is **ABDC**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"There are some backward areas in Andhra Pradesh. Rayalaseema is one of them. Massive degradation of natural resources and extensive changes in land use have resulted in poor crop productivity in Rayalaseema. Soil Organic Carbon (SOC), which is crucial for maintaining soil quality, has decreased by 84% in the region. Poor soil fertility and soil degradation, like in Rayalaseema region, are the major causes of food shortage. The National Soil Survey and Land use planning organisation is doing its job by giving suggestions to the farmers of Rayalaseema. The advice is about which crops are to be cultivated and which not."
